title: WEFT: Scaling Tool-Use Post-Training for General-Purpose Agents
data_curation: MCP tool definitions are built from public tool documentation and business requirements. An environment-synthesis agent infers a shared database schema and execution contracts, then generates FastAPI backends validated with normal and boundary calls and state checks. A task-synthesis agent generates atomic tasks with E2E tests and certifies them by execution validation, tool-chain orthogonality pruning and tool-coverage targets. Coverage-aware sampling over five difficulty profiles (Simple 27% to Expert 12%) composes atomic tasks into cross-MCP DAGs with entity bindings; initial state is grounded progressively in three rounds (entities, relations, distractors). Totals: 8,172 MCPs, 64,755 tools, 41,695 atomic tasks and 11,884 composed tasks (median 20 atomic-task turns). Kimi K3 generates SFT trajectories for all composed tasks. For RL, 1,954 of 5,000 candidate tasks are kept where rubric-judge and executable-verifier scores on 16 Nex-N2-mini pilot rollouts agree under both Pearson and Spearman correlation.
curriculum: Pipeline is SFT then RL from the base models (Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; RL results are reported for 8B and 14B). Data construction is iterative: execution-driven self-evolution runs up to three rounds in which rollouts are attributed, components revised and fresh rollouts re-collected. Training mixtures vary task disclosure (Agentic full brief vs SimUser incremental requests; vague/partial/full explicitness) and harness (ReAct, then OpenClaw, then Hermes) while keeping objectives, dependencies, initial state and completion conditions fixed.
method: WEFT (Whole-system Evolution For Tool-use post-Training) scales the whole agentic interaction system (environment, task, harness, evaluator), not environments alone. Verifiers produce K binary checkpoints from state diffs and tool returns, and the score is their mean. An attribution agent separates policy failures (task kept) from environment, task or verifier defects, and an evolution agent revises only the responsible backend, task graph/state or verifier before revalidation. Prefix-preserving rejection sampling uses atomic-task turns as rejection units, restoring pre-turn state and resampling only the failed task (k=3 retries). Atomic-turn GRPO samples G segments from identical restored states per turn, normalizes binary per-task rewards within the group, applies advantages only to current-turn tokens, and zeroes positive credit for flagged turns (repetition, malformed calls). RL: LR 1e-6, clip 0.20/0.28, K2 KL 1e-3, 131K context, 100 turns, token-level TIS [0.5, 2.0]. MegaMCP shares MCP worker processes across rollouts with copy-on-write private databases and snapshot recovery.
eval_metrics: BFCL V4, tau2-Bench (retail/telecom/airline) and Claw-Eval for main results; Toolathlon-Verified, AutomationBench and Claw-Eval for data ablations, each with its native harness and official metric. WEFT-8B: 52.28 / 62.25 / 35.78; WEFT-14B: 62.21 / 67.63 / 43.77; WEFT-35B-A3B: 63.4 / 74.34 / 64.0 (Claw-Eval below Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's reported 65.4), with 45.99 on Toolathlon-Verified and 26.50 on AutomationBench. Ablations: adding OpenClaw+Hermes harnesses gives a +9.71 mean gain; three self-evolution rounds cut the tool-error rate 1.76% -> 0.96% and add 3.65-5.25 points. Atomic-turn GRPO beats trajectory-level GRPO on tau2-Bench by 5.69 (8B) and 4.43 (14B). MegaMCP cuts sandbox upload by 95.5% and cold-start median time to first tool call by 54.1%.
key_results: WEFT-8B and WEFT-14B beat every evaluated matched-size environment-scaling baseline on BFCL V4, tau2-Bench and Claw-Eval; WEFT-14B exceeds Agent-World-14B by 6.41, 2.23 and 12.27 points. Trajectory-level GRPO regresses tau2-Bench relative to SFT, while atomic-turn GRPO improves all three benchmarks at both sizes (e.g. Claw-Eval +8.54 for 14B).
evolution_note: WEFT responds to environment-scaling work (EnvScaler, Agent World Model, ScaleEnv, Agent-World) by arguing that environments are only one part of the system that generates learning signal; faulty tools, infeasible tasks and bad verifiers also corrupt it. It combines harness diversity (as in ClawGym II and mixed-harness rollouts) with execution-driven repair of environments, tasks and verifiers. Its atomic-turn credit assignment compares segments sampled from identical snapshot states, a finer-grained alternative to GiGPO, PivotRL and BPO.
